subject: [PATCH v4 0/8] mm: fix allocator races with memory hotplug

reviews.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Vlastimil questioned the patch's handling of reserve flags during memory hotplug restarts, pointing out that get_page_from_freelist() is called twice without dropping the reserve flags between calls.

Reviewer Vlastimil pointed out that can_retry_reserves triggers a retry, which drops the nodemask and recalculates preferred zones, suggesting it might not be named well.

The reviewer noted that the patch appears to only partially fix a race condition between memory allocation and hotplug, leaving room for further improvement.

Reviewer noted that patch 5 depends on patch 2 and suggested the commit log needs correction to reflect this
reviews.raw_body:
I don't follow, nothing "drops reserve_flags"? after the restart,
there will still be a get_page_from_freelist() without them followed by
get_page_from_freelist() with them, right?

---

The "goto retry" triggered by can_retry_reserves actually drops nodemask and
recalculates preferred zones. Perhaps "can_retry_reserves" wasn't the best name.

---

So IIUC the allocation was racing with a memory online in a way that it
would fail if the online happened fully after the allocation. So this just
turns part of the race window into the allocation's favor?

---

I mean it's not wrong and if patch 5 depends on it (unless it also only
fixes a racy window in the same way I think is happening here) then so be
it. But the commit log would need correcting.

reviews.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that zonelist_node_idx() still reads the nid from the zone after this patch, and it's not part of the zoneref as they initially thought, so the change is essentially equivalent to just adding READ_ONCE().
reviews.raw_body:
Oh, zonelist_node_idx() reads nid from the zone, it's not part of zoneref as
I thought. So it's the same after this patch, just with READ_ONCE().

Reviewed-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary:
The author acknowledged a concern about reclaim callers not getting a reserve-retry attempt after a restart and agreed to rework the commit message.

The author addressed Vlastimil's concern about the zonelist rebuild, explaining that it rewrites lists in-place and concurrent walks can miss valid zones or pick the wrong zone. The author confirmed that this is a separate issue from the one resolved by their patch.
reviews.raw_body:
"Drops" is the wrong word, sorry.

After a restart the reserve bits are recomputed, but can_retry_reserves
is already false.  As a result no-reclaim/PF_MEMALLOC callers don't
get a reserve-retry attempt (we just exit w/ nopage).

Reclaim callers are fine.

This problem exists regardless of the rest of the series.

But you're right, I will rework the commit message.

---

Not quite - without the online it would have succeeded.  The zonelist
rebuild rewrites the lists in-place, so a concurrent walk can miss valid
zones or pick the wrong zone.  The rest of the series detects more of
these restart scenarios.

Those restarts then exacerbate the issue this patch resolves.  For
example, patch 5 would free a reserve allocation that succeeded - and
then fail because can_retry_reserves is already false.

-- 
~Gregory

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author is addressing concerns about potential conflicts between their patch series and Vlastimil's set of fixes, and has decided to pull patches from Vlastimil's series into theirs to resolve the issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Andrew/David - please don't pull this for now.

We're solving some cross-over between this series and Vlastimil's
set of fixes from anthropic:

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20261027-pgalloc-ai-hotfixes-v1-0-9c7d1aca801e@kernel.org/

Have discussed with Vlastimil, and i'm going to pull patches 4/9 and 5/9
from his series onto this series when i respin this for his updates.
That should keep the backport issues self-contained on this series.

-- 
~Gregory

2026-10-29.patch_summary: This patch series addresses eight issues related to memory hotplug and allocator races in the Linux kernel. The problems include crashes, failures, and incorrect zone or node selection due to concurrent access and rebuilds of zonelists during memory hotplug operations. The patches fix these issues by addressing specific walkers that cause the problems, including allocation routines and memory policy functions. The fixes are designed to be stable and have been tested on a QEMU guest with three NUMA nodes and a 512M pc-dimm left offline at boot. The testing results show significant improvements in performance, with reduced instruction counts and page faults per second.
